newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Strike closes down El Salvador courts.
newsitem.headline: Strike closes down El Salvador courts.

text.p: About 6,000 court workers shut down this Central American country's justice system on Friday by declaring a strike in search of better wages and benefits, labour leaders said.

The protest is affecting all judicial services except for identifying cadavers and investigating sexual assaults "because we can't play games with the the feelings of the families of victims," union leader Jorge Betancour told reporters.
The Association of Judicial System Workers (ASTOJ) said it called for the strike after magistrates on the Supreme Court of Justice on Wednesday denied their petition to negotiate.
The president of the high court, Domingo Mendez, speaking to reporters, assailed the measure and called for a meeting with workers to ask that they "desist from these methods."
The workers are demanding medical insurance for hospital stays, life insurance and overtime pay among other measures.

The ASTOJ started the strike in the capital of San Salvador on Thursday but on Friday extended it to all 14 provinces in the country because of what it considered "inflexibility" on the part of the Supreme Court.
The San Salvador Justice Centre was closed to the public on Friday with signs on the doors saying "we are on strike indefinitely" while police cordoned off the building in a show of force.
